matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to move a stick within the same character to transform it into another valid Roman numeral or operator; many puzzles can be solved by a simple intra‑character change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is invalid, attempt to relocate a stick inside a single symbol before considering moves that affect other symbols.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, check that each resulting character corresponds to a recognized Roman numeral or operator; discard transformations that produce invalid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: After a stick move, ending up with a character that is not a recognized Roman numeral or operator (e.g., a lone diagonal).

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when removing a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining part forms a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider taking a diagonal stick from an X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, possibly creating a new numeral or altering an operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to a numeral, turning '+' into '-' and creating an extra I.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation; an equation that looks syntactically correct must also be arithmetically true.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming all symbols are valid, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Swapping '=' and '-' yields 'XV - XVI = XV', which looks valid but is arithmetically false.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the '=', ensure the equation still contains at least one valid equality sign; avoid removing the only '=' unless you create another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick from the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' turns the original '=' into '-', leaving no equality sign.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., an I), or attached to an existing numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have a spare stick after a move, consider forming a new numeral or augmenting an existing one.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to the numeral VII to create an extra I, turning VII into VIII.

matchstick.title: Swap equality and subtraction operators
matchstick.principle: When both '=' and '-' appear, you can move a horizontal stick from the equality sign to the subtraction sign, turning '=' into '-' and '-' into '=', but you must verify the resulting arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains both '=' and '-', and other moves have failed.
matchstick.example: Changing 'XV = XVI - XV' to 'XV - XVI = XV' by moving a horizontal stick.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After stick moves, ensure each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering rules (e.g., no invalid sequences like 'IXIV').
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming individual symbols are valid, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Forming 'IXIV', which violates Roman numeral syntax.

matchstick.title: Create chain equality by duplicating terms
matchstick.principle: If you can move a stick to turn an operator into a second '=' sign and make all terms on the equation identical, you obtain a trivially true chain equality (e.g., A = A = A).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When other transformations fail and the equation contains an operator that can be turned into '=', consider using a spare stick to duplicate an existing term.
matchstick.example: Failing to consider turning an operator into a second '=' sign, only trying numeral adjustments and missing a solution like 'A = A = A'.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler changes within a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate possible intra‑character stick relocations that keep the character valid before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: When a diagonal is removed from X or V, the remaining single diagonal is not a recognized Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never leave a lone diagonal; either keep both diagonals or use the stick to form a valid symbol.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks syntax but forgets to compute numeric values, leading to syntactically correct but false equations.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After confirming symbol validity, always compute the values of both sides and verify equality.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator changes as a shortcut, overlooking the need for a valid equality sign and correct arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When swapping operators, explicitly check that the equation still contains exactly one valid '=' and that the arithmetic holds.

matchstick.description: Creating nonstandard Roman numeral forms (e.g., IXIV) that are not valid according to standard Roman numeral rules
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may combine symbols in ways that violate Roman numeral ordering conventions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Validate whole numeral strings against standard Roman numeral syntax after any stick move.
